veranderings.voor: leef, en die kewer op die blaar ook
veranderings.na: leef, en die kewer op die blaar leef ook
veranderings.rede: The second part has no verb, so the comma before 'en' is not AWS-correct; repeating 'leef' makes it a full clause and justifies the comma without changing the meaning.
AWS comma before 'en' joining two clauses that each have a subject and verb.

veranderings.voor: maak sy eie kos in sy blare met sonlig
veranderings.na: maak sy eie kos met sonlig in sy blare
veranderings.rede: Afrikaans puts manner before place (TWP order), so 'met sonlig in sy blare' reads more naturally.
'Bietjie vir bietjie' is the usual idiom for gradual change; 'stukkie vir stukkie' suggests piece by piece.
AWS comma before 'en' joining two full clauses, matching the hen sentence just before it.
AWS comma before 'en' joining two clauses with their own subject and verb.
AWS comma before 'en' joining two full clauses.
AWS comma before 'en' joining two full clauses; the protected words after 'en' are untouched.

veranderings.blok: Dinge wat nie lewendig lyk nie
veranderings.voor: waar jy dit nie sien nie
veranderings.na: waar jy dit nie kan sien nie
veranderings.rede: 'Nie kan sien nie' is the natural way to say something is hidden from view.

veranderings.blok: Kieme is te klein om te sien
veranderings.voor: hulle maak nuwe kieme net soos
veranderings.na: hulle maak nuwe kieme, net soos
veranderings.rede: A comma shows that 'net soos ander lewende dinge' applies to all three actions, not only to making new germs.
An animal such as a fish is referred to as 'hy' in Afrikaans; 'dit' reads as if it refers to the head.
'Ding' is vague and wooden for an instrument; 'toestel' is a familiar Grade 4 word.

veranderings.voor: Hoe weet jy die gis leef?
veranderings.na: Hoe weet jy dat die gis leef?
veranderings.rede: Written standard Afrikaans keeps 'dat' here; dropping it is spoken style.

vlae.teks: Elke lewende ding het kos nodig om te werk en te groei.
vlae.rede: 'Om te werk' is vague for a living thing (it may mean 'to function' or 'to have energy'); improving it would require guessing the intended content.
